## Problem

When a new project is created (or an existing one initialized) with an AGENTS.md, the current installer/template behavior emits the full duplicated instruction set as a local file. This is how the four sibling projects ended up with large local AGENTS.md files that duplicate the global one (see SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G, SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N).

## User story

As a developer creating a new project, I want the AGENTS.md installer to emit only the canonical global-reference structure so new projects never start by duplicating the global rules.

## Desired change

Improve the tooling/template that creates AGENTS.md for a project so the generated local file contains only the canonical structure (as adopted by SorraAgents itself in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W):

    ## Global agent guidance

    Read the global agent instructions at ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md — they define the core principles, the Worklog (wl) work-item workflow, and the coding disciplines that apply to every project.

    ## Project-specific guidance

    (project-specific rules are added by the project owner here, never by copying the global file)

- Locate the installer/template mechanism (search scripts, wl/pi project init, templates dir, .pi scaffolding) and change the emitted template.
- The canonical structure is emitted by default; project-specific rules are added by the project owner on top, never by copying the global file.
- If the installer supports an option to copy the global file (e.g. for offline/standalone use), keep it as an explicit opt-in.
- Coordinate with the Worklog side: ContextHub wl init should delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install rather than duplicating it (tracked in ContextHub work item WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The installer/template that creates AGENTS.md now emits exactly the canonical structure above (## Global agent guidance reference + ## Project-specific guidance placeholder).
2. Creating a fresh project (or re-running init) produces an AGENTS.md whose content is the canonical structure, not a copy of the global file.
3. Existing behavior for projects with custom local rules is unaffected (they keep their local rules below the reference line).
4. Any docs describing the installer and the global-vs-project AGENTS.md split are updated.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- TBD at plan time: search for AGENTS.md templates/installers (e.g. ~/.pi/agent/ scaffolding, pi init, project setup scripts). Candidate locations: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json, /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/ (pi's own project init), any templates/ dirs in ~/.pi/agent/.

## Related work

- related-to:SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U (audit session context reduction)
- related-to:SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G (SorraAgents AGENTS.md dedup)
- related-to:SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N (sibling projects AGENTS.md dedup)
- ContextHub: wl init delegation to SorraAgents install (WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514)
data.title: AGENTS.md installer: emit single reference line for new projects

## Goal

As an AI agent or operator, I want the global AGENTS.md to document how to recover from a wiped or corrupted worklog database, so that a future `wl import` incident (or any wipe) is resolved by simply running `wl init` — no custom forensics.

## Problem statement

On 2026-08-11 a `wl import` into the ContextHub worklog store **replaced the entire target database** (~2,800 items wiped), requiring a bespoke SQLite free-page recovery script to restore data. The correct recovery process is simply to run `wl init`, which reinitializes the store. This procedure should be documented in the global AGENTS.md (installed from `~/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`) so agents and operators know the canonical recovery path and the destructive semantics of `wl import`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (installed to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` via `install_pi.sh`) contains a "Recovering from a wiped/corrupt worklog database" section stating the correct recovery process is to run `wl init`.
2. The section warns that `wl import` is **destructive** — it replaces the entire target store — and must only be used with a verified full export/backup.
3. The section documents fallback to `.worklog/backups/*.db` snapshots when `wl init` cannot restore data.
4. The section is picked up by all projects that install the global file (symlinked, no per-project copies needed).

## Constraints

- Documentation only; no changes to `wl` CLI behaviour.
- Keep the section concise (a short procedure + a warning).

## Related

- Incident: ContextHub worklog store wiped by `wl import` (2026-08-11) — recovered via free-page forensics; correct path is `wl init`.
- Work item LP-0MSOI6N3C005VQQT (ContextHub) — the item whose move triggered the incident.
data.title: Document worklog DB wipe recovery (wl init) in global AGENTS.md

discovered-from: SA-0MSMAZP6T007NM0O

# Problem statement

`pytest` is installed at `~/.local/bin/pytest` (Python 3.14, user site-packages) but `~/.local/bin` is NOT on the PATH in non-login shells (e.g., agent tool shells, nohup/cron contexts). Running `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --force` from such a shell fails with "command not found: pytest" — the pytest suite is skipped (returncode null), no green pytest cache entry is produced at HEAD, and the audit skill's automatic full-suite verification is degraded ("Automatic full-suite verification unavailable ... execution-dependent criteria stay partial").

# Observed (during audit of SA-0MSMAZP6T007NM0O, 2026-08-12)

- `python3 -c "import pytest"` succeeds: pytest 9.1.1 at /home/rgardler/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages
- `~/.local/bin/pytest` exists
- Non-login shell: `pytest` → command not found
- Fix on the spot: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` then rerun → suite green (pytest + node, 0 failures)

# Users

- AI agents running `/skill:test` or `run_tests.py` from tool shells
- The audit skill runner, which reads the test cache to auto-verify execution-dependent ACs
- Operators running the test suite from cron/non-login contexts

# Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_tests.py` runs the pytest suite successfully from a non-login shell (no manual `export PATH`) and produces a green cache entry at HEAD.
2. The fix does not break the suite when run from a login shell or when `pytest` is already on PATH (all existing tests still pass).
3. The fix is covered by tests in the test-runner test area (e.g., `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` / `tests/test_test_runner.py`).
4. Running `/skill:test` (or the canonical runner) from the default agent shell at HEAD yields 0 failures.

# Constraints

- Changes limited to the test runner tooling (`skill/test/scripts/`) and its tests.
- Prefer the simplest robust resolution (e.g., `~/.local/bin` PATH fallback or `python3 -m pytest` fallback) — no speculative rework.
- Do not modify agent-infrastructure dirs outside the test skill.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — pytest command resolution
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py` / `tests/test_test_runner.py` — tests for the fix

# Risks & assumptions

- Risk: hardcoding `~/.local/bin` may not apply to other environments. Mitigation: fall back to PATH lookup first, then `~/.local/bin`, then `python3 -m pytest`.
- Assumption: pytest is the canonical Python test runner for this repo (node suites already resolve fine).
data.title: Test runner: pytest not found on PATH in non-login shells

## Summary

Follow-up to SA-0MSLLGDW00098UCC (audit_runner git resolution cwd-dependence), deliberately scoped OUT of that item.

Once git-derived content (file-scope manifest, changed-file list, HEAD sha, working-tree hash) follows the worklog-derived owning project root, the remaining launch-cwd-bound consumers are:

- `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` itself (`_detect_project_root`, audit_runner.py:681) — resolved at import time from the launch cwd.
- Code-quality scan `project_root` (:1536, :1629, :1708).
- Debug-log path (:3645).
- `_repo_index` fallback directory listing (:3007).

## Goal

Make `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` per-audit dynamic (resolved from the worklog store / item prefix like the git pieces), so the documented pattern 'launch the runner from the skill install directory (or any other cwd) and audit items in a different project's worklog' holds end-to-end.

## Design considerations

- Inverts the launch-context guard policy (LP-0MSQ32HNR007AI6B): a launch from a non-owning cwd with a correct `--worklog-dir` becomes legitimate instead of aborting; the guard's fail-fast role shrinks to the undeterminable-ownership case.
- Existing guard tests (skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py) assert abort-on-mismatch and must be inverted/extended.
- Worktree audits (`<owning>/.worklog/worktrees/<id>-<slug>`) must keep resolving to the worktree checkout, not the `--worklog-dir` parent (reuse `_same_git_repository`, audit_runner.py:770).
- Docs: skill/audit/SKILL.md and docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md 'project scope is launch-cwd-only' claims must be rewritten.

discovered-from:SA-0MSLLGDW00098UCC
data.title: Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic (full cwd independence)

data.description:
The audit skill's Phase 1 merge gate (_integrate_into_dev in skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py, ~lines 6099-6109) unconditionally runs 'npm run build' after merging the item's work into an integration worktree (build -> test -> commit order per AGENTS.md). For a repo without package.json / build tooling (e.g. docs-only repos such as AI_Hell), this fails with ENOENT and the gate reports 'Merge gate blocked: integration failed: build failed' -> 'Ready to close: No', demoting the item to open/plan_complete — even though the git merge itself succeeded (rc=0) and the change is valid.

User story: As an operator auditing a docs-only work item in a repo without build tooling, I want the audit merge gate to skip/soften the build step so valid changes can pass Phase 1 without the workaround of committing+pushing to dev first.

Impact: any docs-only item in a repo without build tooling cannot pass the audit merge gate when the work is not yet in dev. Workaround (used for AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V): commit + push to dev FIRST, then audit — _verify_merged_in_dev detects the work already in origin/dev and fails open without attempting the build.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Have an audited work item whose commits are NOT yet in origin/dev.
2. Run the audit on a repo with no package.json (e.g. a docs-only GDD repo).
3. Observe the Phase 1 merge gate fail with 'build error'/'build failed' despite the merge succeeding.

Suggested fix: make the build step conditional on the integration worktree having package.json (or a configured build command, e.g. .pi/test-config.json buildCommand), or record a non-blocking note when no build tooling exists. Mirror the conditional-skip approach already applied to the implement skill's run_build() (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1) and run_tests() (SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

Acceptance criteria:
1. Audit Phase 1 integration succeeds for a repo with no package.json and no build tooling; the build step is skipped and recorded as evidence (non-blocking note), not a failure.
2. Audit Phase 1 still runs 'npm run build' and fails the gate when a package.json with a build script exists and the build fails.
3. Existing merge-gate tests (skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py and related) remain green; a new test covers the no-build-tooling case.
4. Behavior is consistent with the implement skill's conditional build/test skip conventions (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1, SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

discovered-from:AH-0MT94ULUU001NBW3 (AI_Hell work item documenting the audit gate failure on a docs-only repo).
data.title: Audit merge gate hard-codes npm run build; docs-only repos fail Phase 1 integration

data.description:
## Problem

The audit runner's merge gate (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) extracts candidate commit SHAs from work-item descriptions and comments using the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b`. This regex incorrectly matches decimal numbers that happen to be composed entirely of hex digits (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` from a test failure message). The numeric sequence after the decimal point (`2329094824319696`, `231051271500847`) is treated as a valid commit SHA, causing false-positive merge-gate failures.

**Example:** A failing test with the error:
```
expected 0.23290948243196963 to be less than or equal to 0.2310512715008475
```
produces candidate commits `2329094824319696` and `231051271500847` from the audit runner, which then fail to integrate into `dev` because they are not real commit SHAs.

## Root Cause

File: `.pi/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, function `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`, line ~6119:

```python
for m in re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

The `\b` word boundary does not prevent matching within decimal numbers. The sequence `0.23290948243196963` is parsed as a decimal literal, but the substring `2329094824319696` (16 hex chars) passes the 7-40 char hex check.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit no longer extracts decimal numbers as commit SHAs:** The regex in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` must not match numeric sequences that are part of decimal literals (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` → no SHA extracted; `2329094824319696` → no SHA extracted).

2. **Valid commit SHAs are still extracted:** The fix must not break extraction of legitimate commit SHAs:
   - Full 40-hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd3cc78f415afca198930339f2138bed218`)
   - Short 7-39 hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd`, `abc1234`)
   - SHAs in commit messages, WL comment text, and work-item descriptions

3. **Commit SHAs prefixed by `#` (GitHub-style) are still extracted:** `#2c15ebd` or `sha=2c15ebd` patterns should still be detected (the `\b` boundary handles `#` as a non-word character, so the hex sequence is still matched).

4. **All existing audit tests pass:** No regression in the existing audit test suite (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/tests/`).

5. **New test coverage:** Add a test that verifies decimal numbers are not extracted as commit SHAs, and a test that verifies valid SHAs in various formats (full, short, GitHub-style) are still extracted.

## Suggested Fix

Replace the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b` with one that excludes decimal-point-adjacent sequences. Options:

**Option A (negative lookbehind for dot):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<!\.)\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?!\.)", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This uses `(?<!\.)` to ensure the match is not preceded by a decimal point, and `(?!\.)` to ensure it is not followed by one.

**Option B (explicit non-digit-dot context):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![0-9.])\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?![0-9.])", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This is more aggressive — it excludes any sequence preceded or followed by digits or dots.

**Option C (split on dots first, then match):**
Preprocess the text: `text.replace('.', ' ')`, then apply the original regex. This is simpler but could break SHAs that happen to be adjacent to dots in unusual contexts (unlikely but possible in commit messages).

**Recommended:** Option A — targeted fix that only excludes decimal-point adjacency, preserving all other behavior.

## Impact

- **Scope:** Single function in `audit_runner.py` (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`)
- **Risk:** Low — the change is a regex refinement; behavior is identical for all real commit SHAs.
- **Test coverage:** Existing audit tests cover SHA extraction from descriptions and comments; add a test for decimal exclusion.

## Related Work

- N/A — this is a bug in the audit skill's core merge-gate logic.
data.title: audit-runner: decimal numbers incorrectly extracted as commit SHAs in merge gate

data.description:
# Pane title status indicator on skill completion

## Problem statement

When a skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, …) finishes, the operator
cannot tell at a glance whether the pane's work-item session ended cleanly,
needs their attention, or failed. The herdr pane title currently shows only
the dispatch context (e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); the end-of-session
state must be surfaced in the pane title itself.

## Users

- **Operator (producer)** watching a grid of herdr panes: wants a zero-click
  visual signal of which sessions are done, need attention, or failed —
  without opening each pane.

Example user stories:

- "As an operator, when a skill completes cleanly I want a green tick at the
  start of the pane title so I can see it finished."
- "As an operator, when a skill completes but left information for my
  attention I want an orange warning so I know to look at it."
- "As an operator, when a skill cannot complete I want a red no-entry sign
  so I know to intervene."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a work-item skill finishes and produces a final report, the herdr
  pane title (label) for the current pane is updated with a status prefix:
  ✅ (or `Done`) when all ACs are met and no substantive producer content
  exists; ⚠️ (or `Note`) when the skill completed but the report contains
  substantive content for the producer's attention; 🚫 (or `Attention`) when
  the skill cannot complete (any unmet/partial/adjusted AC verdict, or
  abort/failure).
- AC2: The prefix is prepended to the existing pane title (e.g.
  `✅ Manually triggered intake`); no colour/ANSI is embedded in the label;
  the update is idempotent (re-running does not stack prefixes).
- AC3: Text fallbacks `Done` / `Note` / `Attention` are used when emoticons
  are not possible (reusing the report's existing `--no-icons` /
  `WL_NO_ICONS=1` mechanism).
- AC4: On skill abort or failure (including abort paths such as
  `intake.py abort`, `implement.py abort`, audit-runner aborts), the pane
  title is set to the red state regardless of whether a final report is
  produced.
- AC5: The update fails gracefully outside a herdr pane (no `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_PANE_ID`, or herdr CLI unavailable): no crash, no error surfaced to
  the skill run.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and all
  related documentation is updated (SKILL.md reports, tests for the new
  helper).

## Constraints

- Not a pi extension — the update is a call to the herdr CLI/API
  (`herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane id from
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; herdr ≥ current installed version).
- Trigger is skill completion (end-of-session report render), not the agent
  harness lifecycle.
- Status is derived from the final report's content: AC verdicts
  (met/unmet/adjusted/partial), Producer Actions, Notes.
- Orange = "audit passed but there is information for the producer's
  attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action
  is the standard next action in the workflow)" — i.e. substantive content
  beyond the routine workflow next step.
- Colour requirement dropped for text fallbacks: plain `Done`/`Note`/
  `Attention` prefixes, no colour coding.
- Emoji-vs-text fallback follows the existing report convention
  (`--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1`), so both modes stay consistent.

## Existing state

- Every work-item skill ends by rendering a canonical report via
  `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (report skill, SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S),
  passing AC verdicts, producer actions, notes and next action.
- herdr panes carry a `label` field shown as the pane title, set via
  `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane is identified by the
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var (present in pi sessions launched via herdr; also
  `HERDR_ENV=1` and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`).
- `render_report.py` already supports `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` for
  bracketed-text fallbacks — a precedent for the emoticon/text switch.

## Desired change

- Add a small shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`) that, given a
  status (`done` | `note` | `attention`) and the current pane context,
  prepends the corresponding prefix (✅/⚠️/🚫 or Done/Note/Attention) to the
  existing pane label via the herdr CLI, idempotently.
- Integrate the helper into `render_report.py`: after the report is rendered,
  derive the status from the supplied AC verdicts, producer actions and notes
  and update the pane title (done/note states; red when any AC verdict is not
  met).
- Hook the red state into abort paths (`intake.py abort`, `implement.py
  abort`, audit runner abort/exit paths) so failures always surface red even
  without a final report.
- Fail open when not in a herdr pane or herdr CLI is missing.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — derive status from report inputs
  and call the pane-title helper after rendering.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` (new) — shared herdr CLI wrapper: resolve
  current pane, read existing label, prepend status prefix idempotently.
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — abort command sets red pane state.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — abort path sets red pane state.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — abort/failure exits set red pane
  state.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` + `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` —
  document and test the status derivation and pane update.

## Risks & assumptions

- **herdr CLI availability:** assume herdr is installed and the pane env vars
  are set in agent panes (true today — pi sessions launched via herdr carry
  `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`). Fail-open behaviour (AC5) mitigates drift.
- **Existing pane title truncation:** herdr truncates long labels to ~60
  chars (`MAX_PANE_TITLE_LENGTH`); the prefix plus existing label must fit
  within the limit — the helper should truncate the combined string the same
  way to keep the title valid.
- **Scope creep:** wiring red-state into *every* skill's abort path is broad;
  the helper centralises the logic so each abort site is a one-liner. Extra
  opportunities (e.g. coloured labels in the herdr UI itself) are recorded as
  follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Verdict vocabulary:** `adjusted`/`partial` verdicts count as "not fully
  met" → red; `met` only → eligible for done/note.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill": the report renderer this feature extends.
- ContextHub herdr (sibling repo `packages/herdr`): `pane rename`, pane
  titles (`pane-title.ts`, WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), agent-state protocol.
- find-related matches (repo): `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the
  abort/failure paths that must surface the red state; no directly-related
  open work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should this live in the SorraAgents repo as a reusable extension, or be a built-in feature in the pi-coding-agent?" — Answer (user): "It is not a pi extension, it is a call to the herdr CLI/API." Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Q: "Should the title update happen on agent_settled or agent_end?" — Answer (user): "Triggers by the completion of a skill, not by the agent harness." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "To detect a producer notification, check needsProducerReview?" — Answer (user): "The final summary from the skill indicates status." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should the complete title look like?" — Answer (user): "Just add the prefix to the existing title." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Which herdr command sets the pane title?" — Answer (user): "Don't know — look it up using herdr --help." Research: `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>` sets the pane label (pane list `label` field, e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); current pane id from `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; `herdr pane report-metadata --title` is display-only metadata (not the label). Accepted answer: `herdr pane rename` with `HERDR_PANE_ID`.
- Q: "Status derivation from the final summary?" — Answer (user): "Green is correct; Orange is audit passed but there is information for the producer's attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action is the standard next action in the workflow); Red is correct." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where should the herdr call live?" — Answer (user): "(a) inside render_report.py so every skill gets it automatically." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Orange trigger precision — substantive content?" — Answer (user): "Substantive content." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Red path for aborts?" — Answer (user): "Always show red." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Fallback colour mechanics?" — Answer (user): "Drop the colour requirement." Source: interactive reply.

## Summary

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out (many concurrent `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes) ran the test suite with a **leaked `GIT_DIR`** pointing at a live worktree's git dir. Tests that use real `git` (git init/commit/push fixtures) therefore operated on the **live repository** instead of their temp dirs: they committed 24 junk commits (`init`/`Initial commit`, authors `Test <test@test.com>`, `T <t@t>`, `Cache Test`, `RT Test`) on top of the then-current `dev` tip and **pushed them to `origin/dev`**, gutting the branch (483 files, -144,702 lines).

This is the exact incident class documented in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (2026-09-24 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 / docs/dev/test-isolation.md) — the sandbox helper neutralises the vars for test fixtures, but the **production test-execution path does not**.

## Evidence

- Orphaned (`PPID 1`) `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes with env:
  `GIT_DIR=/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.git/worktrees/wl-OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT-nested-node-modules`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core`, `GIT_PREFIX=`.
- Their `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings` children inherited the same `GIT_DIR`.
- `refs/heads/dev` reflog: last legitimate entry `763b8f11` (push by Sorra the Orc), then 24 test commits by `T/Test/Cache Test/RT Test`.
- `refs/heads/dev` and the shared `.git/config` (`core.bare=true`) were rewritten; `.git/HEAD` moved to junk.
- `git ls-remote origin dev` showed the junk tip `6366f913` (fast-forward from `763b8f11`, so the push was accepted).

## Impact

- `origin/dev` overwritten (recovered to `763b8f11` via `--force-with-lease` by the implement session).
- Shared main checkout `core.bare=true`, `dev` ref clobbered (recovered).
- Collateral: another agent's uncommitted work in the main checkout was reset/lost.
- Any push/CI consuming `dev` during the window would have seen the gutted tree.

## Root cause / propagation

- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner` does `env = os.environ.copy()` and passes it to `subprocess.run` **without stripping `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`**. `GIT_DIR` overrides `cwd` for every git subprocess, so fixture `git init/commit/push` hit the live repo.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_run_tests_via_test_skill` -> `run_cached`) have the same gap.
- The origin of the leaked `GIT_DIR` in the launcher is external to `skill/` (no setter found in the repo); the audit fan-out was orphaned. **Defence-in-depth must not depend on the launcher being clean.**

## Proposed fix

1. Scrub `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` (from `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) in `test_cache._default_runner` (and any other subprocess that runs tests) before spawning — single choke point.
2. `run_tests.py`: strip the same vars in its runner/env.
3. `audit_runner.py`: strip before `run_cached`/`run_tests`; ensure per-item audits cannot fan out unbounded (34+ concurrent observed).
4. Regression test: with `GIT_DIR` set to the live repo in `os.environ`, a fixture `git init/commit` must NOT touch  the live checkout (extend `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`).
5. Consider making the live-repo guard fail-fast (abort the run) rather than only post-hoc, and have `run_tests.py` refuse to run when `GIT_DIR`/override vars are present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_cache._default_runner` (and `run_tests.py`/`audit_runner.py`) remove `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG*`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` before spawning tests.
- [ ] Regression test reproduces the leak (fixture mutation under a poisoned `GIT_DIR`) and proves the scrub prevents it.
- [ ] `origin/dev` cannot be moved by any test fixture (asserted).
- [ ] Audit fan-out is bounded (`AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS` honoured; no 30+ concurrent orphans).
- [ ] Full suite green.

## Key Files

- `.githooks/pre-push`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test_cache.py`
- `skill/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_implement_sys_path_resolution.py`
- `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`
- `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`

## Summary

The shared main checkout's git identity was left as the 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident's commit identity (`user.name=T`, `user.email=t@t.com`). `wl sync` refused to merge incoming Worklog data because the author-identity gate rejects commits whose author email does not match the configured `user.email`:

```
✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from
refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 1 incoming commit(s) fail the
author-identity gate.
- ed506bef: author email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com' does
  not match configured user.email 't@t.com'
```

Symptom observed during SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (2026-09-26T23:2x). The identity has since been corrected to the global `Sorra the Orc <250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com>` and `wl sync` now completes, but this item exists to verify the restoration is durable and cannot silently regress (the bad identity came from the incident's `.git/config` rewrite, which is exactly the class SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX guards against).

**Source:** discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX

## Goal

Ensure `wl sync` completes on the main checkout with a correct, durable git identity, so Worklog data is not silently stranded by the author-identity gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git config user.name` / `user.email` on the main checkout resolve to the canonical agent identity (not `T` / `t@t.com`), at local or global scope, and `git config --local --get user.email` returns empty (no incident-era local override).
- [ ] `git config --local --get core.bare` is `false` on the shared checkout.
- [ ] `wl sync` exits 0 and reports success, with a re-run being a no-op (idempotent).
- [ ] A guard/setup check detects and reports a mismatched `user.email` before `wl sync` runs (or in the installer), so the failure is actionable rather than a silent sync refusal.
- [ ] The verification steps are recorded in a comment with the exact commands and observed output.

## Notes

- The incident-era identity is a residual effect of the corrupted `.git/config` documented in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` (recovery playbook §9.4 step 4 verifies identity).
- Do not weaken the author-identity gate; restore the identity instead.

# Summary

The audit runner's Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest omits the audited item's **committed** touched files whenever the working tree is clean, causing false "outside the manifest" / `unmet` verdicts for criteria whose implementation and tests live in those committed files.

Discovered during the audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (log: `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX_20260927T095408.log`).

# Evidence

- The audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX returned `Ready to close: No` with parent AC1 `partial`, AC2 `unmet`, AC3 `unmet` — each justified by wording such as "`test_cache._default_runner`/`run_tests.py` are outside the provided manifest" and "test_cache is outside the manifest so its runner cannot be verified".
- The item's implementation commit `a83ada6a` changed 14 files (`git show --stat a83ada6a`): `.githooks/pre-push`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py`, `skill/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_implement_sys_path_resolution.py`, `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`.
- `git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --name-only` returns all of those files, so the data is available — the manifest simply did not use it.
- The manifest actually used contained only `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`; the latter is **not** in `a83ada6a`.
- The working tree was clean at audit time (`git status --porcelain` showed only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

# Root cause

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:4351`) builds the manifest's file list from:

1. the description's Key Files (`_extract_key_files`);
2. `_git_changed_files()` (`audit_runner.py:4210`) — `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain=v1`, i.e. **working-tree / untracked changes only**;
3. Phase 1 evidence `file:line` refs;
4. a lightweight repo index.

It does **not** use `_resolve_touched_files()` (`audit_runner.py:1476`), which already resolves the union of (a) files in commits referencing the item id (`git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=<id> --name-only`), (b) comment-recorded commit hashes, and (c) Key Files — the correct source for a fully-committed item on a clean checkout.

Consequently, when an item's work is committed and the tree is clean (the normal post-implementation state), `_git_changed_files()` contributes nothing and the manifest collapses to the Phase 1 evidence refs + repo index. The `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` fail-fast guard (`audit_runner.py:1231`) does not abort because the manifest does reference *some* item-repo file, even though it omits the item's actual touched files.

# Desired behaviour

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` must include the audited item's committed touched files (via `_resolve_touched_files()`), so a clean checkout still yields a manifest covering the item's real changes. The fail-fast scope validation must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files.

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_build_file_scope_manifest()` includes the audited item's committed touched files (reuse `_resolve_touched_files()`), in addition to the working-tree diff, Key Files, Phase 1 refs, and repo index.
- [ ] Regression test: with a clean working tree and a committed commit whose message references the item id, the built manifest contains that commit's changed files.
- [ ] A scope-validation regression test asserts that a manifest which references the item repo but omits the item's touched files is rejected (or is impossible to build).
- [ ] Re-auditing SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX after this fix no longer reports its ACs as "outside the manifest" solely because the item's files are committed rather than uncommitted.
- [ ] Full suite green.

# Key Files (predicted)

- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py — `_build_file_scope_manifest`, `_git_changed_files`, `_resolve_touched_files`, `_validate_file_scope_manifest`
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py

# Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — the audit whose false-negative verdicts surfaced this defect.
- Blocks the accurate re-audit/closure of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (dependency edge recorded).
data.title: Audit FILE SCOPE manifest omits a clean tree's committed touched files, causing false out-of-scope verdicts
